name: Detail
grades: A: no errors and at most 1 warning. B: no errors. C: 1 error. D: 2 errors. F: 3 or more. Each rule counts once, however many places it fires. Hints never count.

1.name: Back, close or down arrow at the top

2.name: Item name as a large heading

4.name: Key fact next to the name (price, date, length, status)

5.name: Large photo or video at the top

6.name: Icons at the top right (share, favorite, search, bag)

8.name: Rail or link list of related items below

9.name: Filled button in the bottom third

10.name: Action rows with an icon or chevron

v1.name: Photo first
expect: A large photo or video at the top of the page
A back, close or down arrow at the top
The item name as a large heading
A price or other key fact next to the name

v2.name: Program or recipe page
expect: A back, close or down arrow at the top
The item name as a large heading
A length, date or other key fact near the name

v3.name: Data record
expect: A back, close or down arrow at the top
A key fact such as an amount or status near the top
No large photo; the page opens on text and numbers

not_checked: What the main button, the action rows and the related items open: one screen cannot show the next screen.
Whether the page scrolls, whether the header changes as it scrolls, and what the page looks like further down.
Whether a floating button or pop-up covers content only at one scroll position.

rules.says: The small header text sits on top of the faded page title, so neither is easy to read.
rules.why: The sticky header text sits on top of the faded page title, so neither is easy to read. Seen on 1 of 49 checked screens.

rules.says: A floating button, banner or pop-up covers page content and cuts off a line, a label or a picture.
rules.why: A floating button or pop-up covers page content: the round plus button cuts into the end of a line item on Jobber, and the confirm pop-up hides the start of the title on Apple Fitness. Seen on 12 of 49 checked screens.

rules.says: Footnotes or credit lines are set in very small, pale grey type that is hard to read.
rules.why: Footnotes are set in very small light-grey type that is hard to read. Seen on 3 of 49 checked screens.

rules.says: No price, date, length or status next to the item name.
rules.why: 36 of 49 checked screens have "Key fact next to the name (price, date, length, status)".

rules.says: No block of description text.
rules.why: 30 of 49 checked screens have "Block of description text".

rules.says: The item name is not set as a large heading.
rules.why: 38 of 49 checked screens have "Item name as a large heading". Held at a hint: a second reader agrees on whether it is there on only 57% of the screens read twice.

rules.says: No back, close or down arrow at the top.
rules.why: 45 of 49 checked screens have "Back, close or down arrow at the top".

rules.says: The back, close or down arrow is not in the top third.
rules.why: Of the 45 screens that have "Back, close or down arrow at the top", 45 put it in the top third.

rules.says: The large photo or video is not in the top third.
rules.why: Of the 27 screens that have "Large photo or video at the top", 22 put it in the top third.

rules.says: The icons for share, favorite or search are not in the top third.
rules.why: Of the 25 screens that have "Icons at the top right (share, favorite, search, bag)", 24 put it in the top third.

rules.says: The bottom tab bar is not at the bottom of the screen.
rules.why: Of the 13 screens that have "Bottom tab bar still visible", 13 put it in the bottom third.

rules.says: The filled button is not in the bottom third.
rules.why: Of the 23 screens that have "Filled button in the bottom third", 21 put it in the bottom third.

rules.says: More than one back, close or down arrow.
rules.why: Of the 45 screens that have "Back, close or down arrow at the top", 45 show exactly one.

rules.says: More than one large item name.
rules.why: Of the 38 screens that have "Item name as a large heading", 37 show exactly one.

rules.says: The description is split into separate text blocks.
rules.why: Of the 30 screens that have "Block of description text", 26 show exactly one.

rules.says: More than one large photo or video at the top.
rules.why: Of the 27 screens that have "Large photo or video at the top", 27 show exactly one.

rules.says: More than one bottom tab bar.
rules.why: Of the 13 screens that have "Bottom tab bar still visible", 13 show exactly one.

rules.says: More than one filled button in the bottom third.
rules.why: Of the 23 screens that have "Filled button in the bottom third", 22 show exactly one.

rules.says: A photo-first page with no large photo or video.
rules.why: 19 of 20 Photo first screens have "Large photo or video at the top".

rules.says: Data record screens are not checked for "Large photo or video at the top".
rules.why: Only 0 of 13 Data record screens have it, so position/5 does not apply to a screen of this variant.

rules.says: Data record screens are not checked for "Bottom tab bar still visible".
rules.why: Only 2 of 13 Data record screens have it, so position/7 does not apply to a screen of this variant.

rules.says: Text or a close control is too faint against what is behind it.
rules.why: Accessibility guidelines ask for 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text: 18 pt, or 14 pt bold (button labels are bold). Controls, such as a close or back glyph, need 3:1. Below 3:1 is an error; from 3:1 to 4.5:1 on smaller text it is a warning. Checked on the labels of buttons, the lines of the parts marked as key text, and the close and back glyphs. Not checked on a dimmed screen or over a photo or a pattern, or on the label of a greyed-out button (the guidelines leave out controls that cannot be used yet). Faint placeholder text in an empty field is only a hint, since iOS's own placeholder grey is about 1.7:1.

rules.says: Text is smaller than 11 pt.
rules.why: Apple lists 11 pt as the smallest text size on iOS. Measured from the height of each line, so it is about right, not exact. Checked on the parts marked as key text.

rules.says: A control sits under the status bar or the home indicator.
rules.why: The status bar row at the top and the bottom 34 pt, where the home indicator sits, belong to the system on phones without a home button. Flagged when a control reaches the status bar row or comes within 17 pt of the bottom edge, so a button that only touches the area is not counted.

rules.says: A close or back control is drawn smaller than 13 pt.
rules.why: Apple asks for a 44 x 44 pt tap area. The standard close X in a bar is drawn about 13 to 17 pt across inside that area, so only a smaller drawing is flagged. A screenshot cannot show the tap area itself, so this is a hint.
